answer: Refundable Vertex Deposit. Each identity pays a deposit locked to its first opal-visible transaction, refunded only after sustained participation across distinct counterparties. Cloning forces the attacker to lock fresh capital per clone; honest agents recycle one deposit. The vertex rule caps any single identity at one active deposit, so mass cloning multiplies locked capital linearly. Sybils therefore cost N times the honest float, and each clone must also complete a comet cycle of real trades to reclaim funds.
